summary: As a simulated content creator/developer blogger, I find this idea mildly interesting but not compelling enough to pay for. The pain is real but low-intensity (2/5) and I already have workarounds that are 'good enough.' The market is saturated with partial solutions (Buffer, Publer, Zapier, open-source CLI tools) that cover most of my needs for free or cheap. The one differentiated angle—dev.to integration—is a narrow niche, and developer bloggers are notoriously frugal and comfortable with DIY GitHub Actions solutions. I would not actively search for this, and if I found it, I would not pay more than $5-10/month.
strongest_points: Single source publishing to dev.to + Medium + social + newsletter would save me 30-60 minutes per post if it truly worked with good formatting adaptation
Having a unified calendar view across all channels would reduce my spreadsheet tracking overhead
If it integrated natively with dev.to and had a clean markdown-first workflow, that would appeal to me as a developer blogger more than StoryChief does
weaknesses: Pain intensity is low (2/5)—manual cross-posting is annoying but not painful enough to pay for, especially when I only publish a few times a month
Open-source GitHub Actions + CLI tools already solve the dev.to/Medium cross-posting problem for free, and I'm technical enough to set them up
Existing tools like Buffer ($6/mo) or Publer ($12/mo) cover social scheduling well; adding blog-to-blog + newsletter feels like a marginal increment, not a must-have
Willingness to pay is low (2/5) and developer bloggers are a notoriously frugal segment
Switching friction: I'd need to trust that formatting adapts correctly to each platform—if it mangles my markdown on dev.to or Medium, I'd have to manually check anyway, defeating the purpose
